blocks.text: Condo buildings in Central
Winchelsea — 3738 Norfolk Street and 3733 Norfolk Street

The sub-area's one verified apartment-condo complex, by Adera per current listings ("WINCHELSEA by Adera"), filed expressly under Central BN in the listing feeds. Listings at 3738 Norfolk Street record the building as built in 1993, freehold strata, with in-suite laundry, 2 secure side-by-side underground parking stalls and 1 storage locker for the unit checked, strata inclusions listing gas and hot water, and pets recorded as allowed ("Pets, Yes" in one listing's fields; "Pet friendly building" in another). A building directory records the companion address, 3733 Norfolk Street, as Winchelsea built in 1994, offering elevator, in-suite laundry, storage and wheelchair access. The 1993 vs 1994 year difference between the two addresses is noted, not resolved — the two addresses may be phases of one complex; unit count and the strata's published rental/age restrictions are UNCONFIRMED from the sources checked. School catchments named in the listings are Cascade Heights Elementary and Moscrop Secondary.
Streets, schools and getting around Central

items.t: Central is the civic heart of Burnaby along Canada Way, around Burnaby City Hall, Burnaby Central Secondary and the west shore of Deer Lake. The City publishes no street-by-street written boundary for the MLS sub-area; the area is centred on Canada Way between Willingdon Avenue and Deer Lake — exact MLS boundary streets: UNVERIFIED. City of Burnaby use of "Central" as an official neighbourhood name was not confirmed on a City source.

Where the condo stock concentrates: it barely does. The only verified apartment-condo complex is a small 1990s low-rise on Norfolk Street in the Cascade Heights pocket; the rest of the verified attached stock is townhouses on Norfolk and Smith.

Burnaby community-level context (SnapStats publishes medians at community level only, not for Central): Condos & Townhomes median sale price $686,000, $763/sqft, 98% sale-to-list, 36 days on market in September 2026.

Main streets: Canada Way is the main road through the area, with Willingdon Avenue to the west and Sperling Avenue to the east; Highway 1 runs to the north. Norfolk Street and Smith Avenue carry the verified attached stock in the Cascade Heights pocket.

Transit anchors: there is no SkyTrain station inside the Central sub-area; Metrotown Station (Expo Line) is south-west and Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station (Millennium Line) is north-east of the area. The sourced transit offer is Canada Way bus service between those stations — do not market a Central condo as station-adjacent.
Civic anchors: Burnaby City Hall and the city's governmental and cultural precinct sit in the Deer Lake area at the east end of the sub-area, beside Deer Lake Park, 5435 Sperling Ave.

A self-managed 7-unit strata from 1983 still trades here. Streets, schools and getting around Central

items.t: "Central" is the GVR board sub-area name as used in the SnapStats GVR report for Burnaby: Burnaby's civic heart along Canada Way between Willingdon Avenue and Deer Lake, around City Hall and Burnaby Central Secondary. Street-by-street boundaries for the MLS sub-area are UNVERIFIED — no City or board source read publishes them.
Where the townhouse stock concentrates: the Norfolk Street / Smith Avenue pocket east of Canada Way, facing and near Broadview Park — all four counted complexes sit in that pocket.

Transit: no SkyTrain station sits inside the sub-area; the nearest stations are Metrotown to the south-west and Sperling–Burnaby Lake to the north-east, with Canada Way bus service through the corridor.

Schools: School District 41 (Burnaby) runs 41 elementary and 8 secondary schools with no middle tier (K–7 / 8–12), and catchments are address-based through the SD41 locator. Schools on the Province's list in and beside the sub-area include Burnaby Central Secondary (8–12), 6011 Deer Lake Parkway, Douglas Road Elementary, 4861 Canada Way, Cascade Heights Elementary, 4343 Smith Ave, and Chaffey-Burke Elementary, 4404 Sardis St. Individual listings in the Norfolk/Smith pocket variously name Cascade Heights Elementary and Moscrop Secondary as catchments — listing statements, not locator runs; the locator result for any specific address is UNVERIFIED — check every address.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Central

items.t: Form B diligence (all 4 strata complexes above): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. Listing-level rental/pet lines in are listing data, not bylaws — the Form B and registered bylaws govern. Because each of the four complexes is a separate strata corporation, each requires its own Form B package.

SSMUH (R1): Burnaby's R1 district (consolidated June 2024) allows 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 units on larger lots, and 6 units on lots of 281 m² or more within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop; minimum lot width 10 m, minimum lot area 281 m²; lots with two or more primary units may be stratified; permitted forms include single-family, duplexes, multiplexes, rowhouses and secondary suites. SSMUH speaks to the detached streets around the townhouse pocket, not to the strata complexes themselves.

blocks.text: Good to know about Central

items.t: Burnaby's own tax office sits in this corridor: the City directs mailed tax payments to Revenue Services at 4949 Canada Way — the same street that gives the sub-area its civic character (City Hall is at 4949 Canada Way).

Parkside Greene's marketing point is literal: the complex sits at the end of a cul-de-sac a few feet from Broadview Park and its trails, per its listings — the park frontage is why the complex carries "Parkside" in its name.

Norfolk Street carries three of the sub-area's four townhouse complexes plus its only apartment building (Winchelsea) within a few blocks — Norfolk Terrace (4025), Smith + Norfolk (3868), Parkside Greene (3888) and Winchelsea (3738/3733) — a small attached-housing street inside an otherwise detached, civic corridor.
Burnaby's property-tax penalties cannot be waived by the City even for a one-day-late payment — the City states it has no authority to waive or modify them.

Burnaby rewrote its entire zoning bylaw effective July 1, 2026 (Bylaw No. 14815) and adopted a new OCP on December 9, 2025 — any Central guide or listing sheet still citing the 1965 Zoning Bylaw No. 4742 or the 1998 OCP is out of date.

The only sourced lot figures are the R1 SSMUH thresholds: a minimum lot area of 281 m² and a minimum lot width of 10 m, with the 280 m² / 281 m² unit-count thresholds in. These are zoning thresholds, not a claim about any existing lot's size.

Servicing, as the City states it: Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable, and a residential garbage toter fee; the detached single-family dwelling water charge is $652.33, rates carry a 5% discount if paid by the due date, and for single-family homes sewer is billed as a sewer parcel tax on the property tax notice. Parcel-level servicing for a specific lot: confirm with the City.

ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR split is documented for this sub-area in the research, and no ALR percentage is stated. Parcel-level ALR status is checked in the Agricultural Land Commission's ALR Property and Map Finder.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Central

items.t: Nearby areas: Deer Lake and Deer Lake Place to the east, the Burnaby Hospital area and Garden Village to the south, the Vancouver Heights / Capitol Hill side to the north, and Metrotown to the south-west. Central Park is a separate sub-area west of this one — not to be confused with "Central."

Roads and transit: Canada Way is the main road through the area, with Willingdon Avenue to the west and Sperling Avenue to the east; Highway 1 runs to the north. There is no SkyTrain station inside Central; Metrotown Station (Expo Line) is south-west and Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station (Millennium Line) is north-east of the area. Commute times in minutes: UNVERIFIED.

Parks, library, health: Deer Lake Park, 5435 Sperling Ave, borders the area to the east, with the lake, trails and the city's cultural facilities in the park precinct, and Burnaby City Hall sits in the Deer Lake civic precinct at the sub-area's east end. The library branch serving this area is the Bob Prittie Metrotown Branch, 6100 Willingdon Ave, south-west of the sub-area. The city's hospital is Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St (Fraser Health). No City recreation centre inside the sub-area was confirmed: UNVERIFIED.

Schools: SD41 (Burnaby) operates 41 elementary and 8 secondary schools city-wide, with no middle-school tier — elementary K–7, secondary 8–12. Schools in or beside this sub-area on the Province's list are Burnaby Central Secondary (8–12), 6011 Deer Lake Parkway, Douglas Road Elementary (K–7), 4861 Canada Way, Cascade Heights Elementary (K–7), 4343 Smith Ave, and Chaffey-Burke Elementary (K–7), 4404 Sardis St. School names are Ministry-listed names only.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Central

items.t: Zoning — Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815): adopted Jun 9, 2026 and in effect Jul 1, 2026, replacing the former Zoning Bylaw 1965 (No. 4742), which is never cited as current for Burnaby. Burnaby consolidated its former single- and two-family districts into one R1 Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH) District in June 2024.

OCP — Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan: adopted Dec 9, 2025, replacing the 1998 OCP; it takes precedence over older community-plan land use maps where they conflict. Community plans are adopted by Council as policy guidelines for rezoning and development applications.

Subdivision + servicing — Burnaby servicing-bylaw base number HELD UNCONFIRMED: the former servicing base number was renamed by Amendment Bylaw No. Confirm subdivision and servicing requirements with the City of Burnaby for the specific parcel.

Strata block (for completeness — no Central bare-land strata is verified): Form B diligence (provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws VOID since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a listing's "45+" line is NOT a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Central ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha).

Burnaby property taxes: City of Burnaby property taxes for 2026 were due Friday, July 3, 2026; a 5% penalty applies to outstanding current taxes (and to an unclaimed home owner grant) after the July due date, with a further 5% penalty after the September due date; Council approved a 2.9% property tax increase in the 2026–2030 Financial Plan, about $61 for the average home.

faq.q: Is "Central" the same as Central Park?
faq.a: No. "Central" is the SnapStats / MLS® sub-area for the Canada Way and Deer Lake civic area in mid-Burnaby; Central Park is a separate sub-area around Central Park on the Vancouver border, west of Metrotown (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: What sold in Central in September 2026?
faq.a: Detached: 1 sold from 14 listings (7% sales ratio); condos & townhomes: 0 solds from 8 listings, so the attached sales ratio is not applicable — a very small sample. Burnaby-wide, the median detached sale price was $1,825,000 and the condos & townhomes median was $686,000 that month (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

faq.q: Which schools are in the Central sub-area?
faq.a: Burnaby Central Secondary (8–12), 6011 Deer Lake Parkway, Douglas Road Elementary (K–7), 4861 Canada Way, Cascade Heights Elementary (K–7), 4343 Smith Ave, and Chaffey-Burke Elementary (K–7), 4404 Sardis St; catchments are address-based, so check the exact address in the SD41 locator.

faq.q: Is there a SkyTrain station in Central?
faq.a: No station sits inside the sub-area; Metrotown Station (Expo Line) is south-west and Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station (Millennium Line) is north-east of the area.

faq.q: What is at the east end of the sub-area?
faq.a: The Deer Lake civic and cultural precinct — Burnaby City Hall and Deer Lake Park, 5435 Sperling Ave, with the lake and trails at the sub-area's east edge.

faq.q: What condo stock actually exists in Central?
faq.a: One verified apartment complex — Winchelsea (3738 / 3733 Norfolk Street, by Adera, recorded as built 1993 at one address and 1994 at the other) — plus townhouse complexes (Parkside Greene, Smith + Norfolk, and a small 1983 complex on Smith Avenue).

Current listings say yes — one records "Pets, Yes" in its fields and another calls it a "Pet friendly building." Pet bylaws remain enforceable in BC, so the registered bylaws in the strata package are still the governing document for size/number limits: UNCONFIRMED beyond the listing fields.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Central townhouse or condo long-term?
faq.a: Yes — strata long-term rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022. A Parkside Greene listing independently states "Pets and rental are allowed." Short-term rentals can still be restricted — Smith + Norfolk's developer-era materials say Airbnb-type use is typically not permitted unless explicitly allowed, so read the registered bylaws.

faq.q: What do strata fees cover at Winchelsea, and what should I watch?
faq.a: A current listing's strata inclusions list gas and hot water among the items covered, with trash, maintenance grounds, management and sewer also listed. The watch items in a 1993/1994 low-rise are the depreciation report's envelope, roof and parkade cycles and the CRF balance behind them — both are Form B questions, and no fee level or levy history is published in the sources checked: UNCONFIRMED.

faq.q: Is Central in North Burnaby — what does "-bn" mean?
faq.a: The "-bn" is this site's filing suffix only. The board name is just "Central," and the ground sits mid-city along Canada Way — presenting it as a North Burnaby neighbourhood mis-files it.

faq.q: Can I buy a vacant lot in Central?
faq.a: No verified one — no named bare-land subdivision, bare-land strata or presale lot offering was verified, and much of the sub-area is civic/institutional land around City Hall and Deer Lake that is not market land.

faq.q: How many homes can an R1 lot hold?
faq.a: 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 on larger lots, and 6 on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop; minimum lot width 10 m and minimum lot area 281 m² for SSMUH lots, and lots with two or more primary units may be stratified.

UNVERIFIED for any specific address — no completed SD41 locator run for this sub-area is documented, and pocket listings name different secondaries. The Province-listed schools in or beside the area are Burnaby Central Secondary, Douglas Road Elementary, Cascade Heights Elementary and Chaffey-Burke Elementary; run the exact address in the SD41 locator.
